title: A billing audit can expose crediting uncertainty before a proposed remedy reaches subscribers
source_unit: District of Columbia Public Service Commission docket filings concerning Pepco community-net-metering credit reconciliation and a proposed Solar for All subscriber error-rate remedy; regulatory remedy-stage record, not a customer sample
geography: Washington, D.C.; Pepco, Solar for All subscribers, and community-renewable-energy facilities

crediting_audit_status.value: the audit focused on community-renewable-energy production and did not resolve whether Pepco properly credited subscribers on their electricity bills; required billing data were not provided in time for a core audit purpose

proposed_error_rate_remedy.unit: U.S. dollars per month per Solar for All subscriber for each month of participation during the audit period

institutional_response.value: DOEE/consumer-side parties proposed an error-rate method to make subscribers or facilities whole despite unresolved customer-level billing records

remedy_adoption_and_receipt.value: not established in the cited filings
remedy_adoption_and_receipt.unit: missing final commission adoption, subscriber-level correction, payment or bill credit, adequacy, and later trust or exit

observations.method: DCPSC docket filing review; audit limitation, data-timeliness failure, proposed error-rate amount, and unresolved adoption/receipt are coded as separate remedy stages.
observations.uncertainty: The proposed error rate is not an observed customer loss, final order, or verified payment. The filing describes a regulatory dispute and remedy design; it does not identify affected subscribers, individual months, or final credits.
observations.subgroup: Solar for All subscribers and community-renewable-energy participants during the audit period; exposure may differ by project, participation duration, account, and billing history.
observations.counterinterpretation: An error-rate remedy can be a practical way to compensate when account-level data are incomplete, but it may over- or under-compensate particular customers and cannot be treated as proof that the original credits or later correction were received.

observations.period: June-July billing-error episode; DOEE customer guidance

denominator.unit: customer-guidance route for a reported community-solar billing-error episode

credit_timing_error.value: community-solar credits were front-loaded into June and July statements, producing too many credits on some affected bills

customer_notice.value: affected customers received a debit letter explaining the billing issue

planned_correction.value: DOEE guidance said the September bill would be adjusted to account for excess credits

expected_annual_savings.unit: U.S. dollars per household per year, up to

actual_adjusted_bill_and_later_outcome.value: not observed in the cited guidance
actual_adjusted_bill_and_later_outcome.unit: missing customer-level adjusted bill, correction receipt, adequacy, arrears, trust, and exit

observations.method: DOEE customer FAQ review; the reported billing error, notice, and planned September adjustment are coded separately from verified later receipt.
observations.uncertainty: The guidance describes a planned adjustment, not a verified later bill or customer-level correction. It does not establish how many customers were affected, the amount adjusted for each account, or whether the correction was adequate.
observations.subgroup: Affected Solar for All customers described in DOEE customer guidance; the guidance does not provide a complete affected-customer denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: A customer notice and planned bill adjustment may represent a functioning correction pathway, but without later account evidence the atlas cannot treat the correction as received or sufficient.

related_sources.claim: The related filing describes the unresolved crediting audit and missing billing-data problem.
DOEE customer guidance describes prior community-solar billing errors and a planned bill adjustment.

boundary: This record adds a public-system and consumer-remedy stage from billing-data failure to a proposed error-rate correction. It does not establish the final legal decision, subscriber-level bill correction, cash or credit receipt, adequacy, residual loss, trust, switching, or household energy security. It must remain separate from the project-level monthly-credit receipt record and the program-level household-savings record.
